newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAKS CONCERNED BY CZECH ATTITUDE TO MECIAR TRIP.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAKS CONCERNED BY CZECH ATTITUDE TO MECIAR TRIP.

text.p: Slovakia on Friday expressed displeasure over recent negative Czech statements on a forthcoming visit to Prague by Premier Vladimir Meciar.

"The Slovak side is concerned over the atmosphere in the Czech Republic which is lately increasingly...influencing the preparations (of the visit)," a statement by the Slovak Foreign Ministry issued on Friday said.

The statement comes after some Czech politicians and newspaper called for the cancellation of Meciar's visit, tentatively set for next month, in view of the turbulent political situation in Bratislava.

"It appears that some Czech politicians have, even after four years of the existence of an independent Slovak Republic, been unable to rid themselves of the feeling of superiority and tutalege on the basis of which they comment internal political events in their neighbouring country," the statement said.
It added that the manner in which the Czech politicians have commented "is umpermissible in the relations of two sovereign states".

Some Czech politicians have criticised the behaviour of the Meciar government towards striking actors and students and the recent forcible break-up by police of a sit-in in the ministry of culture by protesting actors calling for the dismissal of Culture Minister Ivan Hudec.
The two countries split and became independent in 1993 after 75 years of life in a common Czechoslovak Republic in which the larger Czech part of the state played the predominant role.

The main purpose of Meciar's visit to Prague is to sign final agreements on the division of property of former common property of the former republic, which has often been the subject of strife between the two neighbours.
"This meeting and its results call for suitable prerequisites and an adequate atmosphere," the statement said.
"The Slovak side remains interested in settling remaining open questions in mutual relations."
